dxgive.evidence_source: [/page/1/Text/4] Berthoz et al. (2013) revealed 55 % of their sample of 38 adults with ASD endorsed symptoms consistent with alexithymia on the Toronto Alexithymia Scale (TAS; Bagby et al. 1994). Additionally our preliminary research indicated 71 % of a sample of 179 adolescents and young adults with ASD also endorsed symptoms consistent with alexithymia.
dxgive.warning: The text indicates participants had a diagnosis of ASD, but does not mention whether they met formal diagnostic criteria for a depressive disorder as an inclusion criterion. The field 'dxgive' specifically pertains to depressive disorder diagnosis.

Source.evidence_source: Toronto Alexithymia Scale (TAS) is a self-report measure; Reading the Mind in the Eyes Task (RMET) is a performance-based task typically administered by a researcher.

MedCat.evidence_source: RMET measures 'ToM difficulties' and 'ability to attribute the mental state of a person', which falls under social engagement (5). The Toronto Alexithymia Scale (TAS) measures 'difficulties with identifying and labelling their emotions', which does not fit clearly into the provided MedCat categories.
